chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibrāhīm al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from Fuḍayl ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī al-Zubayr, from Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Anṣārī, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم commanded us not to eat the meat of the sacrificial animals after three days; then he permitted us to eat, preserve it as dried meat, and send it as a gift to our families.

key_terms.أَذِنَ: granted permission, indicating allowance after an earlier restriction
key_terms.بَعْدَ ثَلَاثٍ: after three days, the time limit mentioned in the initial command
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, the source of the ruling in this report
key_terms.لُحُومَ الْأَضَاحِيِّ: the meat of sacrificial animals offered during the ritual sacrifice
key_terms.نُقَدِّدَ: to preserve the meat by drying it

ai.seo_question: Was it forbidden to eat the meat of sacrificial animals after three days?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم initially prohibited eating the meat of sacrificial animals after three days, then later allowed eating it, preserving it, and gifting it to one's family. It indicates a legal ruling concerning the consumption and use of udhiyah meat and shows a later permission after an earlier restriction.
